fixes.explanation: Walls, baker? I love a sturdy wall, but Moses doesn't build one here. He says the LORD "…will set you high above all the nations of the earth." (Deuteronomy 28:1) That's a promise about being set high, not hiding behind bricks. I'd have picked the walls too, though. I spent years behind a drawer, so I'm a big fan of anything that keeps the dust out.

I see why that sounds right, friend, but Moses never says anything about distance. He says the LORD "…will set you high above all the nations of the earth." (Deuteronomy 28:1) The verse doesn't say Israel will be far from anybody. It says the LORD will set them high above all the nations.

Those sound fancy, friend, but they aren't on Moses' list. He says, "You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country." (Deuteronomy 28:3) City and country, that's the pair. A temple and a palace would look great on a brochure, but Moses didn't put them in this verse.

A cooking pot is a fair guess, baker, and I respect any pot that's put in work. But Moses says, "Your basket and kneading bowl will be blessed." (Deuteronomy 28:5) The kneading bowl is the one he names. As a dough guy, I'm a little offended the bowl almost lost to a pot. I'm fine. Totally fine.

Delayed sounds like a bus schedule, baker, not what Moses says. He says the LORD will cause the enemies who rise up against Israel "…to be defeated before you." (Deuteronomy 28:7) Defeated is much stronger than a delay. These enemies don't just run late, they lose.

Not quite, baker. Moses says the peoples of the earth "…will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you." (Deuteronomy 28:10) The verse gives us awe, and it doesn't mention anyone turning away. They see the LORD's name on Israel, and awe is what Moses says follows.

Manna is a good thought, friend, since the LORD did send it in the wilderness. (Exodus 16:14–15) But here Moses says, "The LORD will open the heavens, His abundant storehouse, to send rain on your land in season…" (Deuteronomy 28:12) Rain is what this verse sends from the storehouse. Manna belongs to a different story.

That's not what Moses says, friend. He says, "Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from any of the words I command you today…" (Deuteronomy 28:14) The warning is about veering off from the words, not about sharing them. Think of a recipe card. You can keep the card in your hand and still wander off from it, and Moses is saying don't wander.
